Find the route across Mars

Turn the red planet in 3D, look inside it, drive a rover, then compare nine landing sites on temperature, water, terrain, radiation, dust and rover access.

Explore the surface, its giant features and its layered interior. Drag to turn the globe, scroll or pinch to zoom.

NASA landings on Mars

Nine NASA surface missions since 1976. Select one to see where it landed (turn on NASA landings on the planner map to see all pins).

Mars vs Earth

Bars show Mars as a share of Earth, using values from NASA planetary fact sheets.

Rover & astronaut 3D view

Drive a Perseverance-style rover across the Martian surface or look closely at an astronaut in a pressurised suit. A Rover Station now stands on the plain in both views.

Drag to turn the view, scroll or pinch to zoom. With the viewer focused, the arrow keys also drive the rover or walk the astronaut. Press R or the Reset button to return to the start position and default camera.

Where the data comes from

Figures are published NASA numbers. Site ratings are qualitative estimates for comparison, not mission-grade measurements.

Read more at NASA Mars Exploration and the Perseverance mission page.

NASA live data connection

Live NASA/JPL Mars Trek MOLA map tiles and NASA Image and Video Library results. Live services require an internet connection.

PDS GEOSCIENCES NODE · MOLA MEGDR

Numerical elevation & local slope

Not loaded

Fetches the actual global MOLA 4 pixels/degree topography grid (signed 16-bit metres) from the NASA PDS Geosciences Node, then samples the selected site's elevation and estimates local slope from adjacent grid cells. This is archived topography, not live/real-time measurement.

Select a site and fetch the PDS MOLA topography grid. If the browser blocks cross-origin access, open this page via the provided local server and check the connection; the result will not be replaced with invented values.

PDS MOLA dataset & labels ↗4 ppd grid label ↗PDS direct file (.img, 2 MB) ↗
Scientific integrity: The color MOLA map is imagery; the numerical panel separately fetches the archived PDS MOLA MEGDR topography grid and estimates local slope from neighboring cells. It does not calculate radiation, temperature, water potential or overall habitability. Existing planner scores remain illustrative and are not silently relabelled as NASA-derived.

About

The team behind RedRoute, built for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026.

FLH Science & Robotics Lab

Established 2024
Explore · Innovate · Inspire

The lab brings robotics, coding and science together. RedRoute is its entry for Challenge 11, where the team built an interactive guide to help people choose where to land and live on Mars.

FLH Science & Robotics Lab · Where to go on Mars and how to survive. Built on NASA open data (MOLA, TES, CRISM, RAD, InSight).

Surface texture: open-source threex.planets project, based on NASA Mars data. Interior layer sizes follow InSight seismic results.
